units.function: open on a global trend before narrowing to the two cities

original_instantiations: a rising share of people in cities is stated first, then the two countries that will feel it most

units.source_excerpt: We used van Rijsbergen's information retrieval effectiveness measure to combine pairs of quantitative measures.
units.reusable_pattern: credit the borrowed tool and the assumption in the same breath
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the source of a borrowed formula

units.function: give the gain and the flaw in consecutive sentences

original_instantiations: the metric is called easy because only census data is needed, then the equal weights are blamed for oversimplifying it

units.source_excerpt: Our metric proves very easy to use: all that is needed is census data that is easily found. On the other hand, we note that our model may be oversimplified.
units.reusable_pattern: balance a claimed ease against the assumption that undercuts it

prohibited_generalizations: do not claim ease without naming the cost

units.source_excerpt: Our growth plan for each city also proved inefficient in accommodating a 50% increase in population in each city.
units.reusable_pattern: end the summary on the shock the plan does not survive
